reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the patch is only relevant for architectures with HVO (Hardware Virtualization On), specifically x86-64, riscv and loongarch, and agreed to make the commit message arch-agnostic.
reviews.raw_body:
Only architectures with HVO matter here: x86-64, riscv and loongarch.
arm64 has had it disabled since 060a2c92d1b6.

riscv and loongarch implement atomic_fetch_add_unless() with LL/SC only,
no CAS variant, so they see the zero at the load. That leaves x86.

I will make the commit message arch-agnostic anyway.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed Peter Zijlstra's concern about the fake head checks on arm64, explaining that dropping RO only removes permission change and not the PFN change, which requires break-before-make. Author also mentioned that James Houghton is working on a solution using an Access Flag trick.
reviews.raw_body:
No. The problem there is the PFN change on a live vmemmap PTE, which
needs break-before-make on arm64. Dropping RO only removes the
permission change.

James Houghton is working on it with an Access Flag trick:

https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261003002123.505555-1-jthoughton@google.com

arm64 will need the writable tail too: its atomic_fetch_add_unless() is
a CAS loop.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch removes fake head checks from the Linux kernel, which are only relevant for x86-64 architecture and a few others. The checks were unnecessary because architectures like riscv and loongarch use LL/SC instructions to implement atomic operations, making the checks redundant. This change simplifies the code and reduces complexity.
